summary:
TRIAD-SYNC is a web-based space-biology and astronaut-health analytics prototype built around a central question: how are changes in sleep and circadian-related measures associated with changes in microbiome and immune indicators in astronauts? It organizes imported observations by participant, mission day, sampling timepoint, biological domain, measured feature, and source. The platform brings together circadian-related measures—sleep, wake, activity, and light exposure—gut microbial diversity and composition, and immune measures including cytokines, inflammation markers, and immune cells.

Users can analyze each domain independently through individual trajectories, group summaries, and raw-data tables, then compare measurements with each participant’s own baseline. Cross-domain exploration uses matched observations from the same person and sampling window, supported by an interactive triad view, pairwise evidence matrix, and astronaut-level timeline. Filters allow exploration by participant, mission-day range, and selected measures. Reports present association strength, uncertainty ranges, evidence grades, source details, and analytical limitations.

TRIAD-SYNC is an exploratory analysis platform, not a diagnostic or medical-prediction system. Synthetic demonstration data remain separate from imported records, missing observations are shown rather than filled in, and observed patterns are presented as associations—not proof of causation.
details:
TRIAD-SYNC was developed to make it easier to explore three areas of astronaut health—circadian patterns, the microbiome, and immune function—within one analytical workspace. Instead of treating different types of measurements as if they were directly interchangeable, the application keeps each system distinct while placing its records along a shared mission timeline. Users can examine each system separately, filter the data by astronaut, mission-day range, or selected measure, and then explore possible links across systems.
The Triad section brings selected measures together through a relationship map, a pairwise explorer, and a combined timeline view. Comparisons rely on records from the same astronaut and sampling window. An optional look-ahead setting also allows users to examine measures from consecutive sampling windows, without presenting them as simultaneous. The Astronaut view follows one individual across the three systems, while the Evidence Matrix displays comparisons between measures from different systems.
The Reports section presents each comparison alongside its evidence level, number of astronauts and paired measurements, link strength, uncertainty range, statistical values, data sources, and analytical limitations. Users can export reports and results in Markdown, CSV, and Excel formats, or print them as PDFs. The Sources section records dataset identifiers, study names, DOI or links, measurement periods, and notes.
The application is built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Plotly.js provides interactive data visualizations, SheetJS supports spreadsheet handling, and JSZip enables ZIP-file handling. The data importer accepts CSV, TSV, TXT, Excel, Word, and ZIP files. It identifies likely participant IDs, timepoints, and measurements, while allowing users to review and confirm how the data should be classified.
A key design decision was to make the strength and limits of the available evidence visible. Filters apply across the application, missing measurements remain missing, and synthetic demo data are kept separate from real-data mode. The system does not claim a relationship when the required records cannot be matched, and it does not interpret an observed association as proof of causation. TRIAD-SYNC is intended as an exploratory research tool, not a diagnostic or medical prediction system.
